valuation_philosophy: My Food Bag is a mature, structurally challenged NZ meal-kit business (single country, single category, high churn, no durable moat, weak competitive position vs HelloFresh's growing NZ reach and the supermarket duopoly). FY2022 EBITDA ($34.2m) was a verified COVID lockdown demand spike roughly 2.1x the current run-rate and is explicitly excluded as an anchor for growth, margins or exit multiples anywhere in this model. The base case is a STANDALONE, no-takeover DCF built from FY2024-FY2026 stabilisation trends, fading revenue growth toward ~1.5% terminal. A live strategic review (Cameron Partners, announced 28-Apr-2026) is a real catalyst that already added ~17% to the share price ($0.21->$0.28) purely on review-announcement speculation, with no outcome, no bid, and the Board explicitly flagging remaining listed as a live option. The bull case reflects a trade-sale/take-private outcome at a modestly higher exit multiple; the bear case explicitly models the review concluding with NO transaction and the deal-speculation premium unwinding back toward the pre-announcement $0.21-0.24 range. Probability weights (25% bull / 45% base / 30% bear) deliberately do not presume a deal is likely.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement / equity movements note (share-based payment expense), NZ$000s converted to millions; verified against H1 FY2026 interim (share-based payments 280 for H1, consistent run-rate)
inputs.lease_treatment_note: FreeCashFlow in the Metrics CSV is already IFRS16-lease-adjusted owner FCF: OCF (13.532) - CapEx (2.872) - lease principal repayment (2.121) = 8.539, verified to tie exactly to the FY26 cash flow statement (also verified for FY24 and FY25). SBC (0.514) is NOT already deducted in this figure (it is a non-cash add-back inside OCF) and has been deducted separately here. Net debt (TotalDebt 2.5 - Cash 0.623 = 1.877) EXCLUDES capitalised lease liabilities by the company's own reported definition (matches the announced '$1.9m net debt'); because owner FCF already charges the lease PRINCIPAL as a cash cost every projected year, the capitalised lease liability is deliberately NOT added to net debt in the terminal EV-to-equity bridge to avoid double-counting the same lease obligation once as an annual cash cost and again as a balance-sheet liability.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest received was only $0.088m against net debt (not net cash) of $1.877m - immaterial, no strip required.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Standard 3yr/5yr CAGRs computed from FY2021 or FY2022 start-years are NEGATIVE or wildly distorted (FCF 5yr -17.4%, NI 5yr +22.3% from a depressed FY2021 base, revenue 5yr -2.25%) because FY2021-22 was a COVID-lockdown demand spike (EBITDA $34.2m FY22 vs $16.4m FY26, ~2.1x). None of these headline CAGRs are used as the growth driver. Instead the model anchors to the FY2024->FY2026 stabilisation/recovery revenue CAGR of 2.43% as the starting point, fading further toward a 1.5% terminal rate given structural category headwinds (HelloFresh NZ reach 72%->84% of population, active customers still ~20-25% below 2021 peak, supermarket duopoly encroachment). Equity CAGR (7.69% 3yr / 5.97% 5yr) is NOT used as the primary growth driver here because the equity build reflects retained-earnings/dividend-payout mechanics on a shrunken FY2023 base, not underlying revenue-generating capacity in a competitively squeezed category.
historical_growth.notes: FCF 3yr CAGR (owner-FCF basis, FY24->FY26) of 65.5% is a base-effect artifact of FY2024 being a trough year (net debt paydown priority, working-capital timing) and should not be extrapolated - it is not used in projections. SBC is small (0.3% of revenue) and stable, so it is not distorting the FCF CAGR materially versus reported FCF.

base.description: Standalone, no-takeover-premium DCF. Revenue growth fades from the FY24-26 stabilisation trend (~2.4%) toward a 1.5% terminal rate, reflecting a mature, competitively squeezed single-country meal-kit category with no assumed active-customer recovery beyond current trends. EBITDA margin holds flat to slightly improving (9.8%->10.0%) as Shop/Ready-Made scales and cost discipline continues, in line with the FY23-26 actual range of 9.6-10.3%. No M&A premium.
base.wacc_rationale: NZ small-cap base 11.5% + micro-cap illiquidity premium 2.25% (thin free float, ~NZ$74m mkt cap, low daily volume) + single-country/single-category concentration premium 1.25% (100% NZ meal-kit exposure, no diversification) + competitive/no-moat + high-churn premium 1.75% (HelloFresh global-scale competitor now covering 84% of NZ population, supermarket duopoly encroachment, active customers still ~20-25% below 2021 peak, zero switching costs) + demonstrated cyclicality (EBITDA range 34.2->16.0 = >2x peak-to-trough) captured within the concentration/moat premiums above = 17.0% stacked WACC.
base.terminal_cap_rationale: Post-COVID (FY23-26, excluding the FY2021-22 IPO-bubble years where the stock traded $0.93-$1.56 on hype) EV/EBITDA range was 2.76x-3.91x, average 3.36x. A 5.0x cap on EV/owner-FCF (not EBITDA) is used as the terminal multiple ceiling - modestly above the historical EV/EBITDA average to reflect FCF being a smaller, more defensible base than EBITDA, while still well below the market's current EV/FCF of ~9.4x (which is inflated by unresolved strategic-review speculation).

bull.description: Reflects EITHER a moderately successful standalone execution (Shop scaling faster, retention gains sustained, GLP-1/health SKUs driving frequency and AOV higher) OR a trade-sale/take-private outcome from the strategic review at a modest strategic premium. The exit multiple (6.0x FCF) is calibrated to a realistic NZ small-cap trade-sale premium over the post-COVID trading range (2.76x-3.91x EV/EBITDA), NOT to the IPO-era 6.5x+ EV/EBITDA multiple, which reflected unsustainable 2021-22 hype.

bear.description: Strategic review concludes with NO transaction (a scenario the Board has explicitly flagged as live) and the ~17% announcement-driven share-price premium unwinds. Simultaneously, competitive intensity (HelloFresh reach, supermarket duopoly) erodes revenue and margin: active customers continue to stagnate/shrink, revenue is flat-to-declining for three years before stabilising, and EBITDA margin compresses toward 8.8% on sustained food-price inflation and price competition.

valuation.note: In all three scenarios the terminal value cap binds, not Gordon growth - at these stacked WACCs (15.5-18.5%) versus 1.0-2.0% terminal growth, Gordon growth would imply an EV/FCF multiple of 5.9x-9.8x, i.e. AT OR ABOVE the current market's implied EV/OwnerFCF of ~9.4x. The 3.5x-6.0x caps, anchored to the post-COVID (FY23-26) historical EV/EBITDA trading range of 2.76x-3.91x (average 3.36x), are what keep the model from silently assuming the market re-rates MFB to a richer multiple than it has ever sustainably traded at outside the 2021-22 IPO-hype years.

base.note: Entry price ($0.198) sits ABOVE base intrinsic value ($0.185) because the 15% IRR hurdle is below the 17% WACC used in the base case - this is the expected relationship documented in the workflow guidance (entry price < WACC-discounted IV only when hurdle > WACC; here hurdle < WACC so entry > IV). The terminal value in this calculation is still the WACC-discounted, multiple-capped terminal value from the base case; only the discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle.
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: The terminal-growth axis is flat across every WACC row because the 5.0x EV/owner-FCF cap binds in every cell tested (Gordon growth exceeds the cap at every WACC 15-19% / terminal growth 0.7-2.7% combination). This is a direct, intended consequence of the conservative multiple cap dominating a small-cap, structurally-challenged business - it means the valuation's sensitivity runs almost entirely through the WACC (discounting) and the interim FCF path, not through an assumed terminal growth/exit-multiple expansion. Terminal growth still matters at lower WACC/higher-growth combinations outside this tested range.

probability_weighted.rationale: Weights deliberately do not presume the strategic review results in a deal - bear (30%) reflects the Board's own explicit caution that continued NZX listing is a live option and 'no certainty that any transaction will eventuate'; bull (25%) reflects a genuine but unconfirmed possibility of a value-unlocking outcome; base (45%, plurality) reflects the standalone status quo, which is what the company will remain absent a concluded transaction.

sanity_check.methodology: 10-year monthly Yahoo Finance price history aligned to 31-March FY-end closes; SBC-adjusted (owner) earnings used on both historical-multiple and implied-multiple sides where applicable (P/E uses reported NPAT since SBC is only 0.3% of revenue and does not materially distort NPAT; EV/FCF uses owner FCF explicitly).

sanity_check.trip_test: PASS - no fix required. Every multiple implied by the base intrinsic value ($0.1854) falls inside or immediately adjacent to the post-COVID (FY23-26) historical trading range: implied P/E 7.07x vs historical 5.38x-8.01x; implied P/B 0.65x vs historical 0.50x-0.96x; implied P/S 0.28x vs historical 0.20x-0.32x; implied EV/EBITDA 3.00x vs historical 2.76x-3.91x. The base case values MFB at a multiple the market has actually paid for the standalone business post-COVID, not at an unprecedented re-rating and not at the IPO-hype multiples. The gap between the base IV and the current $0.29 price is explained by the current price sitting ABOVE the historical multiple range (P/E 11.06x, EV/EBITDA 4.63x, EV/OwnerFCF 9.45x), consistent with an unresolved M&A speculation premium rather than a standalone fundamentals re-rating.
